answer:
**Four-bit weights primarily reduce the amount of weight data that must move.** Compared with 16-bit weights, ideal four-bit storage uses one quarter as many payload bytes, before scales and metadata. At small batch sizes, where weights are read for little arithmetic reuse, that reduction can be very valuable. W4A16 typically retains higher-precision activations and must interpret or dequantize packed weights for computation. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00978) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.17323)

For a simplified matrix multiply, each weight contributes about two FLOPs per input vector. With batch size b and BF16 weights, weight-only arithmetic intensity is approximately b FLOPs per byte. As b increases, the same weights support more arithmetic, so the bottleneck can move from reading weights toward executing the matrix multiply.

**That changes which quantization helps.** A W4A16 implementation may save memory traffic but add unpacking or dequantization work. If arithmetic dominates, those costs can cancel the benefit. W8A8 or FP8 may also accelerate supported arithmetic, subject to hardware and kernel details.

There is no defensible universal batch-size crossover. Shapes, padding, quantization groups, kernel fusion, device generation, and prefill/decode mix all matter. Benchmark the intended workload and quality constraints. Lower memory use can also enable more concurrent requests, so evaluate total serving throughput and latency rather than only one isolated matrix multiplication.

**Technical details and references.**

W4A16 compresses weights to four bits but typically computes with higher-precision activations and dequantized weights. It can speed small-batch decode by reducing bandwidth. W8A8/FP8 also lowers activation precision and may use faster low-precision tensor-core operations. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00978) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.17323)

As batch size grows, each weight is reused for more arithmetic and the workload can become compute-bound. Dequantization overhead may then erase W4A16's bandwidth benefit. There is **no universal crossover batch size**: matrix shapes, kernel fusion, hardware, scales, and quantization format determine it. Some kernels exploit packed weights differently.

Benchmark the intended prefill/decode mixture, not only a single GEMM. Include quality, memory capacity, and concurrency: a slower isolated kernel may still enable higher total serving throughput by fitting more requests.
